observed.facings.png: Three facings drawn at one scale on a checkerboard. South and north show a tall, rounded, barrel-like black body. That body is about as tall as it is wide and fills most of the panel height. East shows a long, low side profile that stands only a little over half as tall as south and north. All three are the same black, deeply wrinkled creature, with a few small knobs along the spine.
observed.south.png: A front view with the face toward the camera. Four yellow eyes glow in two pairs high on the face. A thick, heavy, drooping snout hangs straight down the centre, ending in a rounded tip. The whole body is hung in horizontal fat folds of charcoal-black skin. The four legs are short and pillar-like, with rounded feet. Each foot has several spread rounded toes with pale nails. The rounded hump of the back rises above the head with small knobs on top. The sprite has a clean alpha, no outline and painterly shading.
observed.east.png: A side profile facing right. The body is long and low, shaped like a tapir or pig, with short legs and heavy folds across the shoulder and flank. The head is held low and forward, and four glowing yellow eyes sit in a cluster on the side of the head. A short, thick snout curls down at the tip. There are small knobs or a small crest on the back of the neck. The toes are visible on each foot. The cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: A rear view showing the haunches, the back and a line of three small knobs on the spine. There is no face and no eyes. observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult in three facings: taller and leaner, with longer legs and very long splayed clawed toes. edits.change: All three standing views (front, side, rear) share one ground line and one shoulder height. The side view's back and shoulder mantle rise to the same height as in the front and rear views. The legs are equally thick and the head equally large in every view.

Each of the four feet spreads into broad, individually readable toes, fanned wide apart like the adult's splayed scree-walking feet and scaled down for a young animal. The toes are long and distinct, with dark horn-coloured tips.

The side profile has a deep chest draped in heavy folds, a thick folded shoulder mantle rising above the back, and a long head carried low and forward. The head ends in a heavy drooping snout, with fold-draped skin hanging around the face.

The juvenile proportions are a relatively larger head, a stocky pillar-legged body, and legs shorter than the adult's but tall enough to lift the belly well clear of the ground. The silhouette is built from the folded mantle, the elongated drooping-snout head, the facial drapery and the fanned toes.

request.prompt: A young aveluthia, a tall ponderous pack beast calf from a dark crag land, standing at rest, shown in front view (eyes toward the viewer), side view and rear view (seen from behind, eyes hidden) at one shared scale. All three views stand on the same ground line at the same shoulder height. The leg thickness, head size and body depth match across the views. The side view is as tall as the front and rear views, with its back and shoulder mantle rising to the same height. The body is hung in thick, deeply wrinkled folds of black flesh, with a heavy folded mantle over the shoulders. A deep chest drapes in layered folds, and loose skin hangs in drapes around the face and jaw. The head is long, carried low and forward, relatively large for a young animal. It ends in a heavy drooping snout, a thick muscular hanging nose and lip with a blunt tip. Above the snout, four yellow eyes glow softly, and their warm light falls on the surrounding folds. The body is stocky and sturdy. It stands on four thick pillar legs, shorter than an adult's but tall enough to lift the belly clear of the ground. Each foot spreads into broad, long, individually readable toes, fanned wide apart for walking on loose obsidian scree. The toes are dark horn-coloured at the tips and visible in every view. The palette is black flesh with blue-grey and deep violet-grey highlights in the folds, and soft yellow glow at the eyes. Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, with soft painted edges. Value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one scale. South and north each show a low, wide, dome-backed mound: a mottled slate blue-grey mantle skirt, and on top a raised translucent ridged sac with cream and amber banding. Three short stalks with yellow tips sit at the bottom centre. East is a long, flat, slug-like body in muddy brown-mauve with pale cream oval blotches along the flank. A large, bright lemon-yellow sac with a vein pattern runs the length of the back. Three yellow-tipped stalks point to the right at the head end. The east body colour (brown) and sac colour (saturated lemon) do not match the south and north (blue-grey body, pale cream-amber sac). The north sac is more orange and saturated than the south sac.
observed.south.png: A front view of a low, broad mound. The blue-grey mottled skirt flares out at both sides. A pale, translucent sac with cream and ochre stripes forms the dome. Three yellow-tipped stalks point toward the camera at the base. No eyes. The cut-out is clean, with no outline.
observed.east.png: A side profile of a long, legless, flattish body on one sole. The body is brown-mauve with cream oval patches along the side. A swollen, bright-yellow sac with veins covers the whole back. Three yellow-tipped stalks are at the front (right). The cut-out is clean. No blue anywhere in the body.
observed.north.png: Almost the same silhouette as south: a blue-grey skirt with a faint lilac tint, and a dome-shaped sac in a stronger amber-orange with a cream marbled pattern. Three yellow-tipped stalks still show at the bottom centre. No eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the east facing is about 1.8 cells long and about as tall as the human's torso, low and slab-like. At 32 px/cell the creature reads as a yellow blob on a brownish base. The brown body nearly merges into the brown dirt, but the yellow sac stands out.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult: a pale blue translucent body with a dark outline and a pale-yellow sac, consistent across south, east and north. The adult's north also shows the three yellow-tipped stalks. The silhouette and pose match the candidate's.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head end toward the camera: the three stalks point down and forward at the base, with the sac dome behind.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic shading and translucency. No keyline, not cute, not a 3D render.

OURS.seen: Own art that matches the kept sibling's anatomy. Not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on all facings, with no ground patch or shadow.

request.prompt: A candler variant, a deep-sea creature, for a RimWorld sprite. The body is a slow, flat, slab-shaped mass, wide and heavy, legless, resting on a single broad muscular foot. The skin is soft, damp and slightly glossy. A swollen dorsal sac runs the full length of the spine and bulges above the slab-shaped back. Colouring, identical on every facing: the whole body is a deep slate-blue, a saturated, darker blue than the adult candler's pale blue, with faint lighter-blue mottling; the dorsal sac is a single dark gold, a rich deep amber-gold with soft darker-gold banding. The same slate-blue body, the same dark gold sac and the same mottling appear in the south view, the east view and the north view. The south view is the front view, with the head end toward the viewer and the broad foot below. The east view is a side view: the slate-blue slab body lies in profile, the broad foot runs along the ground and the dark gold sac rides along the spine. The north view is the rear view, seen from behind, showing the back of the slab and the sac with the eyes hidden. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast carry the silhouette: dark gold against deep slate-blue, both clearly readable against the ground. Transparent background. Use the supplied reference only for body shape and proportions; repaint it fully in the deep slate-blue and dark gold palette described here.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South shows the front: a beaked head with eyes, a thick neck, a ridge of knobs rising above it, a wide flat-cornered back slab and four long knobby legs. East shows a long-legged quadruped in side profile with a flat-topped back, a raised hump over the shoulders and a hooked beak on a thick neck. North shows the rear: haunches, a squared flat back slab and the hump behind it, with no face. The palette is pale sandy grey-brown with dark brown mottling. The south facing also has rust-red patches on its shoulders and flanks, which barely appear on east or north. None of the three has an outline.
observed.south.png: Front view. A head with a hooked beak and two eyes faces the camera, set low on a thick, deeply folded neck. A column of rounded knobs runs up behind the head. The back is a flat-topped slab with square corners on each side. The legs are long and columnar, with knobby joints and cloven, hoof-like feet. The hide is pale stone-beige, blotched dark brown, with clear rust-red patches on the shoulders and flanks. The surface has a fine pebbled or cracked texture. The background is clean, with no shadow.
observed.east.png: Side profile, looking right. The back is a long, flat slab with a crusted edge. A raised hump of knobby ridges sits over the shoulders. The neck is thick and wrinkled. The head is narrow and ends in a downturned hooked beak. The legs are long and thin, with knobby joints and split hooves. The hide is pale tan with heavy dark-brown speckled mottling along the back and flanks and only a faint warm tint. Rust-red patches are almost absent. There is no ground and no shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view. A wide, flat-topped back slab overhangs heavy haunches that carry dark pebbled patches. The tail area is small and set between the haunches. The shoulder hump and its knobby ridges show above and beyond the slab. There is no face and there are no eyes. Four knobby legs end in split hooves. The palette is grey-brown with dark mottling and no clear rust red. The background is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the chorn stands several times the height of the vanilla human, with its back about two cells up. At 32 px per cell it is still a clear tall quadruped with a flat back and a beaked head, and it stands out from the tan ground mainly by its darker mottled back and lighter legs.
observed.siblings.png: Reference set labelled RM_Sollak in south, east and north: the same anatomy, pose and silhouette (slab back, shoulder hump, hooked beak, knobby long legs) in a saturated orange-ochre and rust palette with a thin dark edge line. The candidate matches this silhouette and pose closely, in a paler, cooler stone-grey colouring with dark mottling.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the beaked face and both eyes toward the camera, with the chest and front legs below.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the haunches and the back slab from behind. No face or eyes are visible.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera. No facing is a top-down plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 12% (within 15%). In facings.png the three bodies look the same size.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Anatomy matches on every facing: the slab back, the hump and the beak turn with the body. The palette does not match: south carries clear rust-red patches on the shoulders and flanks, while east and north are grey-brown with dark mottling and almost no rust.

SIGNATURE.seen: The slab-flat back, the raised shoulder hump and the hooked beak on a thick neck are all clear in the east profile and readable on south and north.

ALIEN.seen: The tall, camel-like stance is softened by the hooked beak, the squared slab back and the stony knobbed hide. A stranger would not call it a camel at first glance.

DEPARTURES.seen: (1) The hooked beak is present on south and east. (2) The slab-flat back is present on every facing, with square corners. (3) The hide is a stone-like, pebbled, hairless skin, not fur. In this colour variant it reads more grey-beige with dark lichen-like mottling than ochre, and rust shows mainly on south.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with detailed skin texture and a believable joint structure. Not cute, not cel-shaded and not a photo.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art that matches the commissioned chorn anatomy. It is not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: Each facing has a clean cut-out on white or checker, with no ground patch, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The candidate keeps the siblings' anatomy, pose, silhouette and canvas size, and is painted in a clearly distinct, paler stone-grey and dark-mottled colouring. It reads as a colour variant of the same species.

SCALE.seen: It stands far above the human in scale.png, which fits 'towering, long-legged'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a tall quadruped with a flat back and a beaked head, set apart from the ground by its darker back.

request.prompt: A single towering, long-legged grazing creature (the chorn) for RimWorld, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, on a transparent background. Body plan: slab-flat back, a raised shoulder hump, a thick neck carrying a hooked beak in place of a mammal muzzle, long pillar-like legs. Hide: cracked, sun-baked stone, not fur. The coat is one fixed pattern that every facing shares. The base is pale stone-beige with dark-brown mottling and fine cracks. Large, strongly saturated rust-red patches cover both shoulders and both flanks, and extend over the upper haunches. Front view, eyes toward the viewer: the rust-red patches sit on the left and right shoulders and the outer edges of the flanks, with the beak and hump above. Side profile view: the full exposed flank shows the rust-red shoulder patch and the rust-red flank patch, the same size, position and saturation as in the front view, with the dark-brown mottling over the stone-beige base, the flat back in profile, and the beak and hooked tip at the head. Rear view, seen from behind: the back, tail and haunches face the viewer, eyes hidden, with rust-red patches across the upper haunches and on the outer curve of both shoulders, over the same stone-beige base and dark-brown mottling. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. The rust-red, stone-beige and dark-brown distribution is identical across all three facings.

A row of small dorsal spikes runs up the forehead, and overlapping leathery scale plates cover the shoulders. East: a long, low side profile of the same brown animal. It has a boar or pig snout with small tusks, a rounded ear, and shingled flap-like plates along the back with orange-red crack veining. The tail end is spiky, and the legs are short and thick with hoof-like toes. North: the rear, with a tapered stubby tail, plated back and haunches. The ears show at the sides and there is no face. South and north look much taller and bulkier than east.
observed.south.png: Front view, face toward the camera. A pig or warthog face with a ridged snout and porcine nostrils, rounded ears, and a small spike crest on the brow. The body is brown-grey with plates. The alpha is clean.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. It reads strongly as a boar or pig: elongated snout disc, small tusk, upright rounded ear, barrel body. The back carries leathery overlapping scutes with faint orange lava-like veining. The alpha is clean, with no ground shadow.
observed.north.png: A rear view: tail, haunches and the plated back, with the ear tips visible at the sides. There are no eyes and no face. The alpha is clean.

The lower third holds a wavy amber-orange liquid with small bubbles. A cluster of six to eight sinuous pale teal threads hangs from the base. South and north are symmetric and near-identical bladders. East is tilted slightly to the right, and its threads trail down-left. On north the pooled liquid is a duller olive-brown, and the bladder is greyer and less saturated than on south and east. No face or eyes on any facing. Clean alpha.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale: south, east and north of a stocky, short-legged grey-brown quadruped calf. Each facing carries large olive and moss-green mushroom-like caps on stalks rising from the back, with pale flower-shaped speckles on the caps. North is visibly the largest and tallest. East is the smallest and lowest. South shows one large central cap and two lower side caps, left and right. North shows one large cap with a second, smaller cap in front of it, centred over the rump. East shows a large cap over mid-back and a smaller one over the rear.
observed.south.png: Front view. A broad, round-faced calf looks straight at the camera with small brown eyes. The face has a short hippo- or rhino-like muzzle ending in a slight hooked, beak-like tip. There is a row of small blunt knobs and budding horns on the brow, and pale rosette scale patches on the cheeks, shoulders and flanks. The four thick, columnar legs have broad toed feet. Above the body are one big parasol cap and two smaller side caps whose ribbed stalks grow from the back. The background is clean transparent with no shadow.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. A barrel-bodied calf has a rhino-calf head: short horn buds on the nose and brow, a hooked upper lip, a small eye and a skin fold at the neck. There are rosette scale patches on the shoulder and back, and a short, bushy, tufted tail at the left. Two caps on gnarled, root-like stalks grow from the back, a big one over mid-back and a smaller, lower one over the rump. The legs are short and thick. The background is clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view: rump, haunches and a long, smooth, tapering tail hanging down the centre, with no face and no eyes. Above are a large cap and a smaller cap centred over the rear. Small stub-like nubs show at the shoulder sides. The body is wider and taller than in south. The background is clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the east facing sits beside a vanilla human. The calf is roughly three cells long and much bulkier than the human. In normal play at 32 px per cell it reads as a brown lump with a pale-green cap mass on top. The brown hide is close to the dirt colour, and the caps separate it from the ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult gennok. It has long, column legs and a long, narrow, beaked head. Its hide is made of overlapping armour plates. Its three caps are red, orange and ochre: a big central cap on a tall stalk plus two small caps on long stalks, one fore and one aft (and stacked on the south and north facings). The adult palette is warmer and redder than the candidate's olive-green caps.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on, both eyes and muzzle toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows rump, haunches and the hanging tail, with no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are drawn from the low game-camera angle. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 47%. On the shared-scale panel, north's body is wider and taller than south's, and east's legs and body sit lower and read smaller than south's. A profile does not explain north being bigger than south.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: South shows three caps (centre plus left and right side caps). North shows a big cap plus one centred rear cap and no side caps. East shows two caps. The tail is a bushy tuft on east but a long, smooth, tapering tail on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: Broad parasol-like caps on stalks rise from the back and are clearly legible on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The head and body read at first glance as a baby rhinoceros: horn buds on the nose, hooked lip, neck fold and barrel body. Only the back growths and faint scale rosettes depart from that read, so the picture is 'a rhino calf with mushrooms on its back'. The adult's plated hide and long beak, which make the adult alien, are mostly absent.

DEPARTURES.seen: Departure line 'broad parasol-shaped growths rising from its back': present on south, east and north.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with no keylines. The face is soft, as a young animal's face may be, but has no glossy cartoon eyes or toy smile.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art matching the gennok concept. It is not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: A clean cut-out on every facing, with no ground, shadow or halo.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Young proportions are present: big head, short legs, budding horns. Shared species traits (caps on stalks, heavy body) tie it to the adult, but the cap colour and head shape differ; this is noted as a sibling-mismatch finding.

SCALE.seen: Heavy and bulky beside the human, fitting a large pack animal. The game scales the young lifestage down from the adult.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the cap mass on top and the body read as two shapes, though the body's brown is close to the dirt colour.

findings.seen: The head has rhino-calf horn buds, a hooked prehensile lip and a neck skin fold on a barrel body. A stranger names it a baby rhino carrying mushrooms; only the growths depart from that.

reply.subject: RM_Gennok__young
reply.image_seen: Shared-scale panel shows three mushroom-backed quadruped facings; south shows a broad muzzle and horn buds; east shows a barrel body and short legs; north shows haunches and a tapered tail; scale panel places it beside a human; siblings show reddish caps, layered body plates and a beaked profile.

concerns.evidence: East's rounded rhinoceros-like muzzle, horn buds, folded neck and barrel torso read immediately as a rhino calf carrying mushrooms. South reinforces that identification through the broad nostrilled muzzle and stocky legs. The required parasols are prominent, but the underlying animal remains recognizably terrestrial.

The sibling east view has an elongated beaked snout and large overlapping hide plates. The candidate east instead has a short, fleshy rhinoceros muzzle, horn buds and finely pebbled skin. Together with the change from reddish caps to olive caps, these differences obscure the same-species relationship beyond the expected larger head, shorter legs and softer juvenile features.

On the shared-scale panel, north's main canopy rises substantially above south's, and its haunches and legs are bulkier. East has markedly shorter vertical body and leg dimensions. All three are standing with their parasols open; there is no crouch or folded structure explaining the flagged 47% height spread.

South's two lower cap silhouettes could be the exposed sides of the rear parasol visible as one cap in north and east; their central attachment is hidden. East's tail has a ragged edge, but it is not clearly a separate bushy tuft, while north shows a rounded taper. Occluded cap attachments and the existing facing-size discrepancy prevent a confident finding of additional anatomical inconsistency.

edits.change: The calf's head is a long, tapering beaked snout with a hard pale beak tip, set on a stocky body. The skin is overlapping soft hide plates, like layered shingles, across the neck, shoulders and flanks. The brow and nose are smooth and rounded. The calf reads as a young alien plodder, and only its proportions are juvenile.

The parasol caps are red, orange and ochre, with warm gradients from deep red at the rim to ochre at the centre. Each cap sits on a thick, pale, short stalk. This is the adult gennok's palette and stalk form, at calf scale. The hide is a warm grey-brown with darker plate edges, as on the adult.

The calf has one fixed body size in every view. Body height is about 0.55 of the sprite height. Body length in the side view is about 0.6 of the sprite width. The four legs are short and thick, with the same leg length and the same foot width in the front, side and rear views. The front and rear views show the body width of the same body, a little narrower than its side-view length. The feet rest on one shared ground line.

The calf carries exactly two caps. One big cap stands on a stalk at the centre of the back. One smaller cap stands on a stalk over the rear haunches. Front view: the big central cap rises above the shoulders, and the smaller rear cap peeks out behind it, slightly to the rear. Side view: the big cap is over the middle of the back and the smaller cap is toward the tail end. Rear view: the smaller cap is nearest the viewer above the haunches, and the big cap rises behind and above it. The tail is a short, thick tail ending in a bushy tuft of coarse fur. It is shown in the side view and the rear view with the same tuft shape, and it is hidden behind the body in the front view.
Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. All words about outlines or drawn lines are removed from the prompt.

Broad parasol-shaped growths rising from the back are the one departure from a plain animal body, and they stay on a stalk

Calf proportions: rounder body, shorter legs, slightly larger head relative to the body

request.prompt: A young gennok calf, a heavy, thick-hided alien plodding walker, game sprite for RimWorld, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, transparent background, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Three views at one identical scale on one shared ground line: front view with eyes toward the viewer, side view facing right, rear view seen from behind with the eyes hidden. The calf has the same body size in all three views: a stocky rounded barrel body about half the sprite height, four short, thick legs of equal length, and broad flat feet of equal width. Calf proportions: a rounder body, shorter legs, and a slightly larger head than the adult. The head is a long, tapering beaked snout ending in a hard pale beak tip, with a smooth rounded brow and small dark, calm eyes set at the sides of the head. The warm grey-brown hide is made of overlapping soft hide plates, like layered shingles, with darker plate edges across the neck, shoulders and flanks. On its back it carries exactly two broad parasol-shaped caps, each on a thick, pale, short stalk. They are red, orange and ochre, with a deep red rim fading to ochre at the centre and soft pale gills under the rim. One big cap stands at the centre of the back. One smaller cap stands over the rear haunches. Front view: the big central cap rises above the shoulders and the smaller rear cap peeks out behind it. Side view: the big cap is over the middle of the back and the smaller cap is toward the tail end. The tail is a short, thick tail ending in a bushy tuft of coarse fur, with the same tuft shape in the side and rear views. In the front view it is hidden behind the body. The mood is a young animal plodding along, calm and sturdy. Lighting is soft from the upper left, with a gentle shadow tone under the belly.

subject: RM_Gripper__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings of a squat, heavily armoured beetle at one scale on a checkerboard. Its domed carapace is brown, ochre and dark umber, with a faceted, hammered, conchoidal pitting like knapped stone. White granular crust lines every seam: the elytral suture, the pronotum edge, the leg joints. South shows the head head-on, with two dark glossy eyes, mandibles and two thick, clawed forelegs gripping a rusty perforated metal plate. East is a side profile walking right: domed elytra, pronotum, head with eye and mandibles, forelegs clutching the rusty plate in front. North shows the rounded rear of the elytra and the pronotum hump above, with legs splayed and the ends of the plate sticking out at both sides. There is no face on north. Small dark mouthpart tips show beneath it.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. The face looks at the camera, with two black eyes, a central clypeus/horn plate and mandibles. Both forelegs hold a jagged rusty metal scrap with a rivet hole. The pitted brown carapace has white salt crust along the midline and the edges. The cut-out is clean, with no ground.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. Walking legs are spiny and dark-clawed, crusted white at the joints. The elytra show warm amber and brown pitting, with white rime along the suture and the rim. The forelegs grip a rusty plate with a hole, held ahead of the mandibles. The cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view: the elytra split down the middle, the pronotum hump shows behind and above, and the pygidium sits at the bottom centre. No eyes or face. The ends of the rusty plate stick out left and right beyond the body. The legs are splayed. The palette is a slightly cooler, greyer brown than the east facing, and there is less visible white crust.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the beetle is about half a cell long, beside a vanilla human more than a cell tall: a small creature that is still large for a beetle. At 32 px/cell (normal play) the beetle is a tiny brown speck, darker than the sand ground, smaller than the rat.
observed.siblings.png: Reference: the adult gripper in grey/charcoal, with heavy white rime and the same anatomy, pose, silhouette and rusty plate on all three facings. The candidate matches it shape for shape, recoloured in browns and ochres.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head head-on, with both eyes, mandibles and forelegs toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rear of the elytra and the pygidium, with no eyes or face. The only things below are leg and mouthpart tips, the same as in the kept sibling.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera. None is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The bodies read at matching size. Code measured a 14% height spread, which is within tolerance, and it follows the profile/front shape difference the sibling also has.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same carapace, legs and rusty plate appear on every facing. The plate turns with the body: held in front on east, across the front on south, and its ends stick out at the sides on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: The forelegs grip a rusty scrap of metal on every facing, and the pitted flint carapace with salt rime is legible.

ALIEN.seen: The card's earth_body_named is yes (the description calls it a beetle). The flint-knapped pitting, the salt crust and the carried scrap set it apart from an ordinary scarab.

DEPARTURES.seen: Pitted like struck flint: present, as faceted conchoidal pitting all over the elytra. Salt rime at the seams: present, as white crust along the suture, pronotum edge and leg joints (lighter on north). Forelegs clutching scrap: present, a rusty perforated plate. Fist-sized: present, about half a cell beside the human, far larger than a real beetle.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with natural texture and no cute face. There is a thin dark edge line, but it is light and matches the kept sibling. It is not a heavy keyline.

OURS.seen: The art is a recolour of the owner-kept gripper's own art, not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: The cut-out is clean on all facings. There is no ground patch or shadow.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The colour variant reads as the same species as the sibling: identical anatomy, pose, size and silhouette. Its colouring is distinctly brown/ochre against the grey adult.

SCALE.seen: About half a cell, the size of a small dog's head next to the human. That is plausible as fist-sized for drawSize 0.45.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it is a small dark brown oval, separate from the sand ground. It is tiny, but so is the sibling and so is the description's size.

In the rear view, seen from behind, the horn tips show over the first carapace plate, and the carapace, rear plates and hind legs fill the view with the eyes hidden.

Juvenile proportions come from a larger head relative to the body, a shorter and lower stance, and rounder, smaller dome plates. The same body, colours, stone and claws appear in every facing: the front view shows the large head and the broad chest between the shoulder stones; the rear view shows the shoulder stones, the broad back, the haunches and the short tail, with the eyes hidden. request.subject: RM_Sloghog__young

edits.change: The sloghog young is a young version of the adult sloghog. Its hairless pale grey-beige body is built in horizontal armoured bands, with a row of small eyes across the head and many short stubby legs along the underside. Its proportions are softer and rounder than the adult's.

The same species reads at a glance as the adult, with the same pale segmented armour, row of small eyes, many stubby legs and mineral-speckled warts and hooves. Only the proportions are young: a larger head, shorter legs and a rounder body.
The small budding tusks are capped with a rough green-black speckled mineral crust, so the cap reads as a different material from the pale tusk beneath it.
The mineral-crusted tusk tips are large enough to read clearly in the front view and the side view. Rough green-black crust sits on each tusk tip and is speckled on the hooves and the warts.
The back height, body length and body bulk are the same in the front, side and rear views, at one shared scale. The back is low and level in every view.

One rounded barrel body is seen from three sides. The side view has the same barrel girth, depth and low belly as the front and rear views, with short stubby legs in all three. The rear view shows the rear of the body, the back bands and the haunches, with the eyes out of sight.

invariants: Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, transparent background, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette
Pale grey-beige hairless body in horizontal armoured bands
A row of small half-shut, content eyes
Fields of warts down both flanks, speckled with mineral crust
Small budding tusks capped in rough green-black speckled mineral crust
Drawn size matches the 0.85 drawSize; one barrel body shape across all facings
request.prompt: A young sloghog, the juvenile of a poison-grazing refinery hog on a toxic wasteland, for a top-down-angled RimWorld creature sprite. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, on a transparent background, with soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Body: a low, wide, rounded barrel built in horizontal armoured bands. The skin is hairless and pale grey-beige, with a soft warm-grey shadow tone under the bands. The body is round and plump, with a larger head for its size and many short stubby legs along the underside, so the belly sits close to the ground. Legs and hooves are speckled with mineral crust. Head: broad and low, with a row of small half-shut, content eyes across the front of the face and a blunt snout. Two small budding tusks rise from the jaw, each capped with a rough green-black speckled mineral crust over a pale tusk. Both flanks carry dense fields of warts, each wart speckled with the same green-black mineral crust. The colour palette is pale grey-beige skin, green-black mineral speckle and soft warm shadow. The animal looks young, round and contented. The front view has the eyes and mineral-capped tusks toward the viewer. The side view shows the same barrel girth, depth and back height as the front view, with the wart field along the flank and the crusted tusk visible in profile. The rear view shows the back, the banded haunches and the stubby rear legs, with the eyes out of sight. All views are one body at one shared scale, with the same bulk and a low level back.

subject: RM_SumpMouse__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a small brown-grey mouse seen head-on, slightly from above. Its face, round ears, black eyes and whiskers point at the camera, and its tail curls up behind the body. East: the same mouse in side profile, running to the right. The coat is a mottled brown with ochre/orange tortoiseshell patches and a pale belly, and several glossy amber droplets sit on the back. North: the rear view shows the back, the ears from behind, the haunches and the tail curving away to the left. No face is visible. A few small glossy droplets sit on the back. All three facings have very broad, splayed, long-toed pale feet, like snowshoes or gecko pads.
observed.south.png: A front view of a brown-grey mouse: face toward the camera, pink-brown ears, dark eyes, whiskers, a pink nose. The four broad splayed pale feet spread out to the sides and front, and the tail rises behind the body. The camera looks slightly down. Oil droplets are faint or not visible on this facing. The background is clean transparent.
observed.east.png: A side profile of the mouse running right. The coat is mottled dark brown with orange-ochre patches, and the belly is cream. Three or four glossy amber oil beads sit on the flank and back. The long thin pink tail trails left. The broad splayed feet have five long toes each. The background is clean transparent.
observed.north.png: A rear view: the back of the head with both ears, a rounded brown rump, the tail hanging down and curling to the lower left, and the broad hind and fore feet splayed outward. Small glossy droplets show on the upper back. There are no eyes and no face. The background is clean transparent.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the mouse sits in one cell beside the large vanilla human and is a small fraction of the human's size. At normal play (32 px/cell) the mouse is a tiny brown speck on the brown dirt, smaller than the rat comparison.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult sump-mouse: silver-grey coat with white oil droplets, the same three poses (south front with tail up, east running profile, north rear with the tail curling left), the same broad splayed feet, and a slightly darker edge line.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face, eyes, nose and ears toward the camera, with the tail rising behind. This is the same framing as the sibling south.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the ears from behind, the back, the rump and the tail. There are no eyes and no face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: South and north use a slightly raised camera but show the front and rear surfaces, not a rotated top-down view. East is a true profile.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 16% height spread comes from pose: east is a low, stretched running profile, so its visible height is shorter. The body volume matches across the facings. The sibling set shows the same east-lower pattern.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Ears, broad feet and tail match on all three facings, and the tail turns with the body. The palette differs a little: east carries strong orange-ochre mottling that south and north mostly lack (see the polish finding).

SIGNATURE.seen: The broad snowshoe feet are prominent on every facing. Oil beading is clear on east and visible on the north back.

ALIEN.seen: The card says earth_body_named: yes, so the art may look like a mouse. Both departures are present, and the snowshoe feet clearly mark it as not an ordinary mouse.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1. Very broad, splayed snowshoe feet: present on south, east and north, with large five-toed pale pads. 2. Coat beaded with oil droplets: present as glossy amber beads on the east flank and small glossy beads on the north back. The beads are faint on south.

STYLE.seen: Painterly fur texture and realistic anatomy. The eyes are small and dark, not glossy or cute. No heavy keyline; the thin edge darkening matches the siblings.

OURS.seen: The anatomy and poses match the owner-kept sump-mouse siblings. This is not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean transparent background on all facings, with no ground patch, shadow or halo.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it is a small elongated shape. Its brown colour sits close to the brown dirt, so it reads mainly by size and silhouette. Contrast is weaker than the silver-grey adult's (polish).

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. All show the same pale cream, shaggy-furred animal on four thin stilt legs with dark hooves. The coat has olive-green moss-like streaks along the back and neck, plus black brush-stroke stripes. A small spiky rust-red comb runs along the back, and a small red tuft-crest sits on top of the head. The south and north facings are about the same height. The east facing is a little shorter because the neck arcs forward.
observed.south.png: Front view. A small narrow head faces the camera, with two dark slit eyes, a small muzzle and a red spiky crest on the crown. A long, straight, furry neck rises out of the chest. Short rust-red spines show on both sides of the neck base at shoulder height, fanning out sideways like a ruff. The chest and front legs are toward the camera, and the hind legs show behind them. The legs are long and thin, with dark cloven hooves. The cut-out is clean, with no ground under the animal.
observed.east.png: A true right-facing side profile. The long neck makes an S-curve up and forward, and a small narrow, beak-like head with a dark eye points right. A row of rust-red triangular spines, short and low like a budding sail, runs along the mid-back. Green moss streaks run along the spine and neck, and black streaks cross the flank. The rump ends in a short fluffy tuft with no distinct long tail. The legs are long and thin with a backward-bending hock. Painterly fur texture, no outline, clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: fluffy cream haunches and rump, with the hind legs toward the camera and the forelegs visible beyond. A narrow rust-red comb runs up the midline of the back and continues up the back of the neck to the red head crest. The back of the head shows no eyes and no face. There is no distinct tail, only a fluffy rump. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom (140 px per cell) the candidate is about 1.5 cells tall and taller than the vanilla human. At 32 px per cell the pale animal still reads as a long-necked, long-legged shape beside the human and the rat, but the pale coat has only modest contrast against the tan ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult vellak, south, east and north. The coat is smooth and short, tan and cream with darker tan blotches. A large rust-red fan sail with radiating ribs stands on the back. The tail is long, bushy and dark brown. The head has a backswept crest or horn-like tufts. The neck is a long S-curve and the legs are long stilt legs. The adult has no green and no black streaking.

edits.change: The coat is smooth and painterly, in a warm tan base with soft darker brown blotches, the same coat as the adult vellak. The fur lies short and even, with soft painted edges. Value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

The narrow head carries the adult's recognizable swept crest, angled back along the skull. A dark, bushy tail is developing at the rump, shorter and fluffier than the adult's. The proportions are juvenile: a slightly shorter neck, a larger head for the body, long thin stilt legs and a small sail. Young and adult read as one species by one artist.

The south view is a front view, with the eyes toward the viewer. The rust-red sail-comb is one narrow midline crest rising straight up behind the base of the neck. The neck partly hides its lower edge. It is the same single dorsal fan as in the east and north views, seen end-on, as a thin vertical ridge on the centreline.

The body stands on exactly four legs in every view. In the south view two forelegs stand in front, spaced under the chest, and two hind legs stand behind them, partly hidden by the forelegs and body. Each leg is one connected stilt that runs from the body down to a single hoof. In the east view the four legs show as two near and two far, in a walking stride. In the north view two hind legs are in front and two forelegs are partly hidden behind them.

invariants: Body plan: a tall quadruped on four stilt legs with hooves, with no shoulders to speak of. The body draws straight up into a long boneless furred neck that carries a small narrow head at the tip.
One rust-red sail-comb stands along the dorsal midline, fanned open, in the same colour and the same position in every facing. It is small on the young.
Warm tan blotched coat, the same palette as the adult, with a dark bushy developing tail.
Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges.

Facings: east is a side view with the head toward the right of the image. North is a rear view seen from behind, showing the back, tail and haunches, with the eyes hidden. South is a front view with the eyes toward the viewer.

Body: a small, slender four-legged walker covered in overlapping segmented plates of pale grey-white ice, with glowing pale-blue cracks running between the plates. The palette is cool blue-grey with pale blue light in the seams. The back is plated in a row of small ice scales. The legs are slender and shorter than the adult's, ending in narrow ice-hard feet. The body has the proportions of a young animal: a smaller frame and a larger head. The same body depth, body length and leg length hold in every view, so the animal is one size from the front, side and rear.

Head: narrow and beak-like, built of ice plate. Six pale, milky-white eyes sit in a small cluster set into the sides and crown of the beak. Two small budding antler nubs of pale crystal rise from the brow, and a few small crystalline frills line the neck.

Static: faint pale-blue arcs of crackling static run along the plate seams and flicker at the antler nubs and frill tips, a soft glow.

Views: the front view shows the beaked face with the six pale eyes toward the viewer, the chest narrow and the two front legs slender. The side view shows the long profile: beaked head, plated back, four slender legs, a short plated tail. The rear view, seen from behind, shows the plated back, haunches and tail, with the eyes hidden.

A single creature, centered, filling the frame, on a transparent background.

reply.subject: RSW_Bolotaur__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one checkerboard at one shared scale. South: a squat four-legged reptile facing the camera. It has a spiky pale crown, an open toothy mouth, a cream belly and splayed clawed forefeet. East: a long low-slung lizard-like body in right profile. It has a raised neck, a head with an open mouth and fangs, pale spikes along the crest and back, and a long striped tail trailing left. North: the same body from behind. Pale spikes run down the back of the head and spine, the haunches and hind feet face the viewer, a short tail tip points down between the legs, and no face shows. South and north are similar in height; east is lower and much wider.
observed.south.png: Front view of a heavy, wide reptile. The head is broad and carried low, with a pale cream spike crown around it, dark eyes, an open mouth with reddish gums and two pale fangs, and cream-green folded skin on the throat and chest. The shoulders are dark green with bold black-green bands across the forelegs. The forefeet are large and splayed, with long pale-tan claws. A pointed belly or tail tip shows between the legs. The background is clean transparent, with no ground or shadow.
observed.east.png: Right profile. A low quadruped with thick legs and big splayed clawed feet. The moderately long neck curves up to a blunt head with an open red mouth and fangs. Short pale spikes run from the head along the neck and back to the tail. The back is dark moss-green with lighter green mottling and large pebbly plates. The underside is pale cream-green. The long tail has dark bands. The scale texture is painterly and there is no outline. The cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Pale spikes are visible at the back of the head, and a row of pale chevron spikes runs down the spine to the tail base. The broad rump and the backs of the thighs are dark green with lighter banding. A cream underside shows between the legs, and a short tail point aims down. Four splayed feet with pale claws show at the bottom. There are no eyes and no face. The cut-out is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 4 cells long beside the vanilla human, much bigger than a person, plausibly rideable. At 32 px per cell it still reads as a long green lizard-shape with a pale crest, clearly apart from the tan ground, and far larger than the human and the rat.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult bolotaur in south, east and north. It has the same anatomy, pose, spike crown, open fanged mouth and splayed claws. Its colouring is a plainer, more uniform olive-yellow-green with a creamier belly and little banding.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face toward the camera: eyes, open mouth, throat and chest, with both forefeet forward.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the head spikes, a spinal spike row, the rump and the hind feet; there are no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are drawn from the low game-camera angle, and none is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured height spread is 12%, within 15%; south and north look the same bulk in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The spike crest, banded dark-green hide, cream belly and pale claws appear on every facing. The crest turns correctly: it is a crown around the head on south and north and a lengthwise row on east.

SIGNATURE.seen: A large, long-necked reptile that is clearly big enough to be a mount (east and scale.png).

ALIEN.seen: Lizard-like, but the heavy squat body, pale spike crown and fanged wide mouth make it read as a fantasy reptile rather than a stock iguana. It is the same body as the owner-kept adult.

CANON.seen: Squat four-legged body with thick legs and splayed feet; a thick neck with folded throat skin; a broad blunt head carried forward; a long tail. Dark moss-green back and limbs; a cream-green belly; pale crest spikes from the head over the neck; long pale-tan claws; reddish gums under a heavy brow; pebbly scales. It is not a sauropod, has no shell and is not tan.

STYLE.seen: Painterly scale texture with soft lighting and no outlines; not cute and not a 3D render.

OURS.seen: Own art that matches the owner-kept adult's style; not vanilla or donor art.

ALPHA.seen: All three facings sit on clean transparency, with no ground patch or shadow.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the siblings. The colouring is distinct: darker moss-green with bold dark banding on the limbs and tail, against the adult's plainer olive-yellow.

SCALE.seen: About 4 cells long beside the human, a large rideable reptile.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the long green body, pale crest and cream belly stand apart from the tan ground.

proposals: The variant's colour difference from the adult is mostly in value and banding within the same olive-green hue. At 32 px in a mixed herd, the two looks may be only mildly distinguishable. A stronger banding contrast, still within the canon's dark olive/moss-green, could make the herd variety more visible.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of a slim, long-legged orange reptilian quadruped at one scale. South: the front view, with a spiky fan of crest spines around the head, a long pale-tan throat and a curled fin-tipped tail at the left. East: a full side profile walking right, with a long upright neck, a swept-back spiny crest, a long snout and a scaled body with a darker ridge of spines along the back. The tail sweeps down and back to a broad, curled, fin-like tip. North: the rear, with a narrow ridged crest seen from behind, the darker spinal ridge down the neck and back, and the tail hanging down the centre to a fin-tipped end. All three are on transparent ground.
observed.south.png: Front view. The face looks at the camera, with purple-ish eyes, two forward nostrils on a short-looking foreshortened snout and small teeth showing in a slight grin. A radiating fan of rust-red spines frames the head on both sides. The long neck has a tan throat. The chest is deep and the four legs are long and thin, ending in dark rounded hoof pads. The tail curls out to the viewer's left, ending in a broad, ribbed, fin-like blade. The rendering is painterly, with fine scale texture, and there is no outline.

The hide is rust-orange with a paler tan belly and legs. The legs are long and slender, with dark hoof-like pads. The tail is long, drooping and curled at the end into a broad, flat, ribbed blade. The alpha is clean and there is no shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The back of the head shows the crest as a narrow vertical ridged fan, with no face or eyes. A darker red spinal ridge runs down the neck and spine into the tail, which hangs down the middle and ends in a broad fin-like tip. The haunches are rounded and the four thin legs have hoof pads. The alpha is clean.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate stands about as tall as the vanilla human sprite and is several times longer than the rat. At 32 px per cell it still reads as an orange long-legged lizard-runner silhouette, with crest and tail visible, against the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult dalgo has a larger, darker semicircular crest, long curved lower tusks, heavier muscle and darker red shading, and a tail with a large upturned blade. request.prompt: A young dalgo, a tall rust-orange carnivorous reptile from Onderon, drawn as a RimWorld creature sprite on a transparent background. The style is painterly, realistic and vanilla RimWorld, with soft painted edges and soft top-down lighting. Value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Body: a lean upright reptile in rust-orange with a paler cream-orange belly and throat and darker rust-brown dorsal shading. It has long, strong running legs, a slim neck, a narrow wedge-shaped head with forward-facing eyes and a toothed snout, and a long tail that ends in a broad, flat, blade-shaped tip. Because it is young, its head is slightly large for its body, its legs are slightly shorter than an adult's, and its crest is small. Crest, one fixed design for every view: a single thin, flat, ridged fan-plate stands upright in the head's centre plane. It rises from one attachment line along the crown, from between the eyes back to the base of the skull, and sweeps back and up toward the neck. The plate carries 5 to 6 evenly spaced ribs that radiate backward from the attachment line, with a scalloped trailing edge and slightly darker orange-brown colouring than the head. Because the plate lies in the centre plane, its width changes by view. The east view (side view) shows the plate broad, a swept-back fan along the head's length. The south view (front view, eyes toward the viewer) shows the plate edge-on, a narrow ridged fan rising behind the crown, with the head and snout wide and visible in front of it. The north view (rear view, seen from behind) shows the same narrow plate with its trailing edge and stacked ribs in a narrow column rising above the back of the skull, over the back, haunches and tail with the eyes hidden. Keep the crest the same size, colour, rib count and attachment line in every view. The tail with its blade tip stays the same size and shape in every view.

request.prompt: A gelagrub, a large insectine ground grub native to the jungle world Felucia, drawn as a RimWorld creature sprite. Body plan: one big, heavy, soft segmented grub body, long and rounded like a fat caterpillar, with a smooth rounded head end carrying a small dark mouth and two dull dark eyes, a row of short stubby legs tucked under the flanks, and a tapering rear end. The body stays in its grub state for its whole life: no wings, no adult carapace. The flanks are olive-green with soft moist skin and gentle segment creases. Along the whole back runs one dorsal ridge of broad amber-orange panels, each panel separated from the next by a dark green dividing band; the panels have warm amber-orange interiors with subtle darker orange shading. This dorsal ridge keeps the same amber-orange panels, the same dark green bands and the same olive-green flanks in every facing. Front view (south): eyes and mouth toward the viewer, the amber-orange ridge visible running up over the head and shoulders, same amber-orange panels and dark green bands as the side and rear views. Side view (east): body in profile, the full amber-orange ridge along the top with dark green bands between the panels. Rear view (north), seen from behind: the tapering rear end and the amber-orange ridge running away along the back, eyes hidden. Consistent palette in all facings: olive-green flanks, amber-orange dorsal panels, dark green bands, a pale muted olive-cream underside. The body is built of broad soft shapes; soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, transparent background, the animal filling most of the frame.

observed.south.png: Front view, with the face toward the camera. The hide is slate grey-lavender with large dark purple blotches on the shoulders and flanks. The horns are cream with pale blue-teal streaks and black tips. Pink ears are tucked between the horns. Small blue eyes sit high on the head. The beak is dark purple and hooked, under a magenta crest. The chest is white and shaggy. The legs are thick pillars ending in white shaggy feet with dark claws. observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The body is massive, with an arched back and a hump over the shoulders. The head is held low on a thick neck. The hide is blue-grey with dense dark purple-grey spots that thicken toward the spine, and the belly is pale. Dark indigo spikes run along the spine. The long white tail has a purple streak and droops to the ground. The feet are white and furry with black claws. The art is painterly and realistic, with wrinkled hide. The alpha is clean.

observed.facings.png: Three facings of one yellow, striped, reptile-like quadruped on a checkerboard. All three use one shared scale. South: front view. The red-capped face with its red snout looks at the camera and has grey-ringed eyes and drooping flaps on each side of the head. The body is tall and fills about 430 px of the panel height. East: side profile facing right. The tail is long and tapers, held low, the back is gently arched, the neck is moderate and the head is red-snouted and held at shoulder height. The legs are fairly short. The whole animal stands only about 245 px tall, much smaller than the south and north views. North: rear view. The tail points down toward the camera, a blue-grey mottled spine runs along the back, and the top of the red head and its flaps show above the hump. No face shows. North is about 415 px tall, close to south.
observed.south.png: Front view of a golden-yellow reptile with orange-brown vertical stripes on the flanks and a pale cream, wrinkled throat and chest. The head is narrow with a red face cap that runs into a pinkish-red tapered snout, pale blue-grey rings around the eyes and two small brow nubs. Skin flaps hang behind the jaw. Four columnar legs end in reddish three-toed clawed feet. The background is clean alpha and painted with real lighting and skin folds.
observed.east.png: Right-facing side profile. The body resembles a hadrosaur's: a long, heavy tail held straight out and low, and a moderate hump over the mid-back with blue-grey mottling and orange stripes. The neck is short-to-moderate and the face is drawn out, ending in a red bill-like snout. There is a grey eye ring, a flap behind the head and a pale belly. The legs are moderately slender with visible knees, and the feet are reddish and clawed. The animal is small inside the canvas and the background is clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: haunches, with the tail tapering down toward the viewer and a pale underside on the tail. The back carries blue-grey mottling along the spine, with orange stripes on the flanks. Above the hump only the top of the red crown and the two ear-like flaps show, with no eyes and no face. The hind feet are reddish. The background is clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate is about 2 cells long, about as tall as the human figure's head-and-torso and longer than the human. At 32 px/cell it reads as a small yellow-orange quadruped with a red-tipped head, about twice the rat's size and comparable to the human.
observed.siblings.png: The adult jamel, kept by the owner: gaunt, with very thin, stilt-like legs, a tall arched hump over the shoulders, a long neck hung forward with the head low, the same golden hide with orange stripes and blue-grey spine mottling, a red face cap, a grey eye ring, a long tail and dark red-brown clawed feet. A faint dark edge runs around the silhouette.

SAME_SIZE.seen: At the shared scale the east animal stands about 245 px tall against about 430 px for south and about 415 px for north, which matches the measured 128 vs 220/210. SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Every facing has the same palette, stripes, blue-grey spine mottling, red face cap, head flaps, tail and reddish clawed feet, and each structure turns with the body. The difference in leg proportion between south and east is covered under SAME_SIZE.

SIGNATURE.seen: The red bill-like snout on the long face, the yellow hide and the hump are legible on south and east.

ALIEN.seen: The nearest look is a juvenile duck-billed dinosaur, not a camel. The hump, red face cap, grey eye rings, neck flaps and striping keep it from reading as a familiar living Earth species. The card's camel departures are present.

DEPARTURES.seen: (1) Long face ending in a red bill: present on south and east. (2) Yellow bare skin, not fur: present, a wrinkled reptilian hide. (3) Spindly legs: only partly present. STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic hide with folds and soft lighting, no keyline, no cute face. The eyes are small and set naturally.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art in the jamel palette that matches the kept siblings, not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on every facing. No ground patch, no shadow, no backdrop.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Young proportions are present: a relatively large head, shorter legs, a smaller hump and softer features. The animal reads as the same species as the adult through its palette, face cap, eye ring, flaps, tail and feet.

The side profile has its legs fully extended under the body, so it stands as tall as the front and rear views, with the same leg length and the same gap between belly and ground. Flat, even lighting from above and slightly in front. Transparent background.

observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. South is a round orange-red body seen head-on. It has a huge gaping mouth ringed with sharp white teeth, a pink-red tongue and a small drip-like stub under the chin. Six glossy dark eyes sit in a 3-over-3 cluster on top of the head. There are two large pale-blue translucent veined wings at the upper sides, two smaller translucent lobes at the lower sides and two small nubs behind the head. East is a right-facing profile of a plump fish-like body with the open toothy mouth, the tongue out and the eye cluster on the brow. One large translucent wing rises up and back, a second sweeps down and back, and a small forked pair of translucent tail fins sits at the rear. North shows the rear: a smooth round orange back with a lighter belly at the bottom, two large translucent wings and a thin vertical translucent blade down the centre, which is the tail fins seen edge-on. North has no face and no eyes.
observed.south.png: Full-resolution south. Front view, face toward the camera. Six eyes, a wide toothy maw, a tongue and a chin stub. Four translucent wing lobes: a large upper pair and a smaller lower pair. Wet, smooth painterly skin with a lighter belly. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Full-resolution east. True side profile looking to the screen's right. Fins and wings are translucent with visible veins. Two small tail fins at the rear form a vertical fork. The body is limbless. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Full-resolution north. Rear view of the back and haunch: no face, no eyes. The large wings look somewhat taller here than on south. observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about half a cell long beside the human, about bird-sized. At 32 px per cell it is a small orange speck with pale wings, about rat-sized or smaller.
observed.siblings.png: The adult neebray, a reference. It has the same red-orange body, lighter belly and pale-blue veined wings, a row of small eyes across the brow, a wide toothed mouth with a red interior and a chin tendril. request.prompt: A bird-sized juvenile neebray, a space-dwelling creature of Tatooine, Rugosa and Rishi Moon, drawn as one sprite sheet of consistent views (south, east, north) of the same animal. The body is limbless, smooth and tapering, like a soft muscular spindle, with no legs, arms or feet. It carries six eyes in two rows on the front of the head. Two large translucent wings, one on each side of the body, show fine veins and a pale tint, and are seen through to the ground behind them. Beneath each large wing sits a smaller lower wing lobe, so the wing set is a large upper wing and a smaller lower lobe on each side. At the rear of the body, two distinct smaller tail fins spread sideways, one to the left and one to the right, with the rear centre of the body visible between them. The wing set and the tail fins are identical in size, shape, attachment point and angle in every view. South view: front view, eyes toward the viewer, the large upper wings and smaller lower lobes splayed sideways, the two small tail fins spreading sideways behind. East view: side view, the near wing and near lower lobe in profile, the two small tail fins spreading sideways from the rear. North view: rear view, seen from behind, showing the back of the body, the haunch end of the body and the eyes hidden; the large upper wings and the smaller lower lobes sit at the same size and the same height as on the south view, and the two smaller tail fins spread sideways left and right from the rear centre, matching their attachment and angle in the south and east views. Palette stays the same in all views: the same body colour, the same wing tint and the same fin tint. Transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette.

The creature is calm and grazing, with its head held low. Facings: the front view shows the head with eyes and mandibles toward the viewer; the rear view, seen from behind, shows the tail end and the row of glowing pods along the back, with the head hidden; the side views show the full ringed profile with the pod row along the top. subject: RSW_Ronto__variant

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard: south, east and north of a huge four-legged long-necked saurian. It wears a leather saddle, a bedroll, saddlebags and a bridle with reins. Its hide is greenish olive with dark stripes on the neck, back and tail. All three facings are about the same height. The palette differs by facing: east is the palest, a light sage and cream; south is a mid olive-grey-brown; north is the darkest, a deep olive green with heavy dark blotches on the haunches.
observed.south.png: Front view. The triangular head faces the camera, with a short horn on top and a pointed nose horn above a downturned beak. Two large cream wing-like ear flaps fan out from the sides of the head. The long neck comes straight toward the viewer and has a cream throat and dark bands. A breast strap and harness run to the saddle. The body is broad, with deep wrinkles at the knees and wart bumps on the shoulders. Four columnar legs end in broad clawed feet. The cut-out is clean, with no ground.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The S-curved neck rises to a beaked head with a grey nose horn, an eye and a bridle, and a cream ear-flap frill sweeps back. The hide is pale sage-olive with darker banding along the neck, back and tail. The belly is cream. Wart bumps are scattered over the flank. The knees are heavily wrinkled. The tail is short and thick. There is a saddle with a bedroll, a coiled rope and saddlebags, plus a girth strap. The cut-out is clean.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The thick striped tail hangs down the centre between broad haunches. The neck rises away from the camera, and the ear flaps and the horn tip show from behind. No face or eyes are visible. The saddle and bedroll are seen from behind. The hide is dark olive green with dark blotches and bumps on the haunches and wrinkled legs. The cut-out is clean.

observed.facings.png: Three facings shown at one scale. South and north are large, tall, rounded masses that fill most of their cells. East is a long, low profile whose body is visibly about half as thick as the south and north views. The palette is rust-orange and clay-brown, with large dark-ringed eyespots on the segments and pale curved tentacles at the head. The rendering is painterly and realistic, with no keylines.
observed.south.png: The front view of a fat, segmented grub-like animal facing the camera. The head sits at the centre, with two small dark real eyes and a radial mouth ringed with small teeth. About twelve pale, cream, horn-like curved tentacles ring the head: some point up, some hang down like tusks. Behind the head, the domed body is wider than the head and shows two large ochre-ringed eyespots on its flanks. Stubby ringed prolegs stand at the bottom. The background is transparent, with no ground or shadow.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. About five body segments run left to right, each with a large staring false eye: a dark pupil inside a pale ochre ring inside a dark band. The head is at the right, with a small real eye, a toothy mouth, and pale curled tentacles above and below the mouth. Rank after rank of short ringed prolegs stand underneath. The body fills the canvas width, but its height is only about 40% of the canvas. The background is transparent.
observed.north.png: A rear view looking along the back from behind and somewhat above. The blunt rounded rear end is at the bottom, with a pair of anal prolegs. Segments recede upward, each with paired eyespots on its flanks. The tips of the pale tentacle crown show beyond the far end. There is no real face, mouth or real eyes: only the false eyespots, which belong to the back. Many prolegs show along both sides. Because the body recedes up the canvas, this view is the tallest facing.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the creature in east profile is about one cell long and sits lower than the human's shoulder: a small, low crawler. At 32 px per cell, it reads as an orange segmented worm with a pale head fringe.
observed.siblings.png: The adult SandPillar reference is a flat, dull grey-brown blob in a different style, with a heavy black keyline. It has hood-like head flaps and small black eye marks. It has no eyespots, no tentacle crown and no visible prolegs. The south view is compact and upright, the east view is a humped worm with its head raised, and the north view is a wide rounded rump.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head head-on: real eyes, mouth and tentacle crown face the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the blunt rear end and the back segments. The only eye-like marks are the description's false eyespots on the back. There is no real face or mouth, and the tentacle tips show beyond the far end.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: No facing is a straight overhead view. North is an elevated rear view, with segments receding up the canvas, which fits the angled camera for a long body. A second look could confirm that north does not read as top-down.

SAME_SIZE.seen: East's body is about 170 px thick, without legs. On south and north, the same body is about 330 px thick and about 300 px wide. East shows the animal at roughly half the scale of the other two facings. The measured spread is 119%.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same palette, eyespots, pale tentacle crown, toothy radial mouth and ringed prolegs appear on all three facings. The crown is drawn around the head on south and east, and its tips show beyond the far end on north, so the crown turns with the body.

observed.facings.png: Three views at one scale on a checkerboard. South shows a tall, long-necked quadruped walking toward the camera, face forward, with two pale ringed horns that curve up and back. East is a full side profile walking right, with the neck raised high, a small antelope-like head, horns swept back over the poll and a long thin tail ending in a dark tuft. North shows the rump and tail from behind, the back of the neck and the ears, and the horn tips with no face. The coat on every view is pale sandy tan with broad warm rust-brown crosswise bands over the neck, body and legs. The silhouettes and heights match closely.
observed.south.png: Front view. A narrow pale face with dark eyes and a muzzle looks at the camera. Rust bands run in chevrons down the neck and across the chest. Two pale cream horns curve outward and back in a lyre shape. The legs are banded and the hooves dark, and the tail swings out to the viewer's left with a dark brush tip. The cut-out is clean with no ground patch.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The neck is long and sloped, the withers high and the back slopes down to the hindquarters, as in a giraffe. The head is small and deer- or antelope-like, with ears and two long pale horns hooked backward. Broad rust bands cross the neck, shoulder, barrel and legs, and the belly is pale. The tail is long and thin with banding and a dark tuft. The rendering is painterly-realistic with soft fur texture and no outline.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Rump, banded tail hanging with a dark brush, banded hind legs, the back of the neck with stripes, and the ears and horn tips at the top. No eyes or face are visible. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human the zeer is very tall: the human reaches only about the zeer's knee to belly, which fits a 4.6 m browser. At 32 px per cell it reads as a tall striped long-necked silhouette with the pale horns visible, distinct from the brown ground.
observed.siblings.png: The owner-kept adult zeer has the same anatomy, pose and silhouette on each facing: the same lyre horns, long neck, tufted tail and gait. The adult's coat is a warmer mid-brown base with many thin, dense dark-brown tiger stripes. The candidate is clearly a colour variant of it: a paler sand base with fewer, broader, rust-red bands.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The face, eyes and muzzle look straight at the camera, and the chest faces forward.

NORTH_REAR.seen: Rump and tail toward the camera, the back of the neck and the ears and horn tips only, no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are standing views from the game's oblique camera. None is a dorsal plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured height spread is 2%. The facings panel shows matching heights.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same horns, banding, tufted tail and leg proportions appear on all facings. The horns turn correctly: lyre-shaped from the front, hooked back in profile, tips seen from behind.

SIGNATURE.seen: The long neck and the rust-banded tan coat with pale back-hooked horns are legible on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The giraffe proportions are canon ('giraffe-like quadruped'). The crosswise tiger bands in place of patches and the long swept-back antelope-like horns in place of ossicones make it read as a different creature, not a giraffe. The look is closer to a hybrid than to a plain giraffe, matching the kept adult.

DEPARTURES.seen: First departure: tan coat crossed by rust-brown bands, not patches. Present on all facings. Second departure: two pale horns hooked back, not ossicones. Present, clearest on east.

CANON.seen: BODY PLAN: tall, long thin neck, small head, long thin legs and tail. Yes. COLOUR LAYOUT: tan base with rust crosswise bands on neck, shoulders and legs, and the horns are the palest element. Yes. HORNS: a pair of thin, curved, swept-back horns. Yes. NEGATIVE: no blotch pattern, no ossicones, not stocky. Yes.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic fur shading with no keyline outline, no cute features and no glossy cartoon eyes. It sits in the same rendering register as the siblings.

OURS.seen: Bespoke art matching the owner-kept adult, not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard. No ground patch, shadow or halo under the hooves.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Same anatomy, pose, size and silhouette as the adult siblings on each facing, in a distinct colouring: a paler sand base and fewer, broader rust bands against the adult's dense thin dark stripes. It reads as the same species.

SCALE.seen: The zeer towers over the human (the human reaches about knee or belly height), which fits a 4.6 m tall browser.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the tall neck, the banded body and the pale horns read as bold shapes against the brown ground.

proposals: The broad, high-contrast bands on this variant lean slightly toward a 'zebra-striped giraffe' read. A future pass could break the bands with slight irregularity so they read less like an Earth zebra pattern, as a polish note only.

request.prompt: A juvenile ulvassk, a young airborne scavenger of the cracked flats, drawn as a RimWorld creature sprite in painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, on a transparent background. It is the younger stage of the adult ulvassk and has the same body plan in smaller, softer juvenile proportions. The body is a long, flat, shallow sac of thin translucent skin, wider than it is tall, with an almost level roof, a gentle swell and tapering thin front and rear edges. Warm light passes through the skin, most visibly near the vane edges, and faint internal ribbing and a soft glow of heated air show inside. The sac is slung between two pairs of membrane vanes. The vanes are short, ribbed like a kite and stretched on pale, slender, hollow bone spars that look soft and not yet hardened. The membrane is a pale amber-grey with warm translucent edges, and the spars are bone-cream. Below the sac hangs a compact cluster of jointed, hook-tipped feeding limbs, slightly short for the body, folded around a radial mouth. There is no head. Along the leading edge of the sac runs a ring of dark pits, set a little large for the body, and they take the place of eyes. Views: the front view shows the leading edge with its ring of dark pits toward the viewer, the vanes spread to both sides, and the feeding limbs hanging beneath. The rear view shows the trailing edge of the sac and the backs of the vanes, with the limb cluster folded beneath and the pits hidden. The side views show the long flat sac in low profile, with both vane pairs stretched out and the limbs hanging below. Soft painted edges; value and colour contrast against the ground carry the silhouette. The creature floats, hanging from its sac, and does not stand. Weathered earth and ochre ground tones sit beneath it.
